name: Emily's Lebanese Deli
whatItIs: Lebanese deli opened in 1973 by Emily Awaijane, near St. Maron church; known for tabbouleh, kibbeh and grape leaves.
evidence: Listed at this address in an Aug. 22, 2025 ranking based on July 2025 Yelp data. History from the Northeaster, Oct. 21, 2021. The deli's own website did not load.

name: Zakia Deli
whatItIs: Deli opened in 2007 by David Maalouf, named for his mother; Lebanese, Greek and American menu.
evidence: Racket review dated March 19, 2025, describes a recent visit and lists hours; also in an Aug. 2025 Stacker ranking.

name: Beirut Lebanese Street Food & Catering
whatItIs: Fast-casual Lebanese restaurant and caterer opened by John and Madelaine Khoury after 41 years in West St. Paul.
evidence: Own site has a current menu, catering packages and online ordering for the Rosemount address; February 2025 roundup reported the opening. Listed as a 2026 St. George festival sponsor.

name: Beirut Restaurant (West St. Paul)
whatItIs: Long-running Lebanese sit-down restaurant.
evidence: February 2025 roundup refers to it as West St. Paul's 'former' Beirut Restaurant, with the owners now in Rosemount.

name: Massad's Grille
whatItIs: Massad family restaurant known for chicken shawarma ('schwarma') sandwiches; sells bottled sauce.
evidence: Own site lists hours and online ordering; KEYC, May 22, 2026, says Mankato's mayor has run the Massad Group since 1984.

name: Najwa's Catering
whatItIs: Catering company of the Massad family, over 20 years in the Mankato area.
evidence: Own site with phone for consultations (undated); part of the Massad Group, which KEYC reported on May 22, 2026, as still run by Mankato's mayor.

name: Olives
whatItIs: Restaurant listed by Massad's Grille as one of the Massad family businesses.
evidence: Named on the Massad's Grille site; its own website returned an empty page.

name: Sweet Lou's Craft Sausage and Butchery
whatItIs: Butcher shop, breakfast and lunch counter and food truck owned by Louisa Farhat, whose extended family is in Lebanon.
evidence: Own site lists current hours (Tuesday to Sunday) and the St. Louis Park address. MPR News, Oct. 30, 2024, interviewed the owner about Lebanese Red Cross fundraising.

name: Mocol's Supermarket
whatItIs: Family corner grocery opened in 1917 by a Lebanese immigrant; run by the third generation in 2017.
evidence: Mankato Free Press 2017 centennial story and Blue Earth County Historical Society 2021 post describe it operating; no 2025 or 2026 page found.

name: Cedars Hall at St. Maron
whatItIs: 5,600-square-foot parish hall rented for weddings and events, with a 42-by-42-foot dance floor.
evidence: Northeaster, Dec. 2, 2022. The parish website showed only a placeholder on Oct. 31, 2026.

name: Ray J's American Grill
neighborhoodOrCity: Minneapolis (500 Central Ave. SE, per 2021 report)
whatItIs: Restaurant and bar founded by the Lebanese American Jacob brothers and run by Michael Jacob's sons in 2021.
evidence: Northeaster 2021 and a Dec. 2022 Northeaster mention; no own site or 2025-2026 page opened.

name: Nye's
neighborhoodOrCity: Minneapolis (112 E. Hennepin Ave., per 2021 report)
whatItIs: Bar operated by Rob and Tony Jacob, sons of Lebanese American restaurateur Michael Jacob, as of 2021.
evidence: Northeaster, Oct. 21, 2021. Its website returned no content.

name: Jacobs Trucking
whatItIs: Family trucking business that, by the Northeaster's account, grew from Tom Jacobs's ice wagon.
evidence: Historical mention only (Northeaster, 2021).

name: Estephan Engineering
whatItIs: Engineering firm; its owner, a St. Maron parishioner born in Ijdabra, Lebanon, organized a 2017 parish fundraiser.
evidence: Own site loads with project and service pages but shows no date or address. Owner identified in The Catholic Spirit, March 23, 2017.

name: Jacob's 101
whatItIs: Bar bought by the Jacob brothers in 1971; an after-school hangout for Northeast teachers.
evidence: Northeaster 2021: run by the brothers until 1991, then by a nephew until 2005.

name: Abdo's Store
whatItIs: Neighborhood store of Naiff and Fadwa Abdo, one of Mankato's first Lebanese families.
evidence: Blue Earth County Historical Society: closed in 1980 after almost 70 years.

name: Holy Land (grocery and deli)
whatItIs: Middle Eastern grocery and restaurant the Northeaster lists as serving Lebanese, Syrian, Egyptian, Palestinian, Afghan and Iranian customers. Not described as Lebanese-owned.
evidence: Northeaster, June 3, 2021; no newer page opened.

name: Northeaster
whatItIs: Neighborhood paper that has covered Lebanese Northeast's history, St. Maron and its festival.
evidence: Publishes 2026 event listings, including the Sept. 2026 St. Maron Lebanese Festival listing linked here. Not a Lebanese-owned outlet.

name: St. Maron Lebanese Festival market
whatItIs: Lebanese store, gift shop and food sold at the yearly parish festival.
evidence: 2026 festival listing (Sept. 18-20, 2026) mentions a Lebanese store.

name: Byblos Lebanese Grill
whatItIs: Business listed as a corporate sponsor of the 2026 St. George Middle Eastern Festival.
evidence: Named on the festival's sponsor page; its listed website returned an empty page and no address was found.
